automotive-ev-battery.title: Kia is recalling over 21,000 EV9 SUVs over a faulty airbag issue
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Kia has initiated a safety recall affecting more than 21,000 EV9 SUVs due to a defective airbag system that may fail to detect child occupants in the front seat. This recall addresses a critical safety concern for one of Kia's flagship electric vehicles.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Nickel exposure at CATL plant in Hungary
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Hungary's occupational safety authority suspended operations in three areas of CATL's Debrecen battery plant after nine employees were identified with elevated nickel exposure. The incident compounds ongoing production challenges at the facility, which has already faced delays in ramping up cell manufacturing capacity.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Study highlights potential solutions to economic barriers in battery recycling
automotive-ev-battery.summary: A European study reveals that EV battery recycling currently operates at a loss of approximately €1.90 per kilogram of battery pack despite advanced technical capabilities. Researchers propose revised business models and enhanced processing efficiency as viable pathways to achieve economic viability in the recycling sector.

automotive-ev-battery.title: VW's €20,000 electric car likely to be named ID. Up
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Volkswagen has finalized the naming of its planned entry-level electric vehicle, to be called the ID. Up rather than ID.1, according to industry reports. The model is scheduled for launch in 2027 with an anticipated base price of approximately €20,000, targeting the mass-market EV segment.

automotive-ev-battery.title: BYD reports 10,000 Flash Chargers installed in China
automotive-ev-battery.summary: BYD has announced the installation of 10,000 Flash Charger units in China, reaching the halfway point of its target to deploy 20,000 stations by year-end. The T-shaped charging stations feature dual charging cables and deliver 1,500 kW of charging power, supporting rapid EV charging infrastructure expansion.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Drivn to deploy 150 electric heavy-duty trucks in India
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Drivn, an EV leasing platform based in India, has partnered with Tata Motors to deploy 150 electric heavy-duty trucks across the country. The initiative represents a significant step toward electrifying India's commercial transportation sector through collaborative leasing solutions.

automotive-ev-battery.title: UK order books are open for Chery's first all-electric SUV
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Chery's L6 EV, the brand's inaugural all-electric SUV, has opened order books in the United Kingdom with an expected delivery window in early Q4 2026. The vehicle offers up to 279 miles of range and is available across two trim level configurations for UK customers.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Mahle launches e-compressor production in India
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Mahle has inaugurated an electric compressor manufacturing facility in Coimbatore, India, with an anticipated annual production capacity exceeding 300,000 units. The electric compressors are critical components for thermal management systems in electric vehicles.

automotive-ev-battery.title: Hubject advances Plug&Charge in Japan in collaboration with Plugo
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Hubject, the Berlin-based EV roaming specialist, has partnered with Japanese charging infrastructure company Plugo to advance Plug&Charge technology adoption in the Japanese market. The collaboration aims to streamline seamless, automated charging authentication across Japan's EV charging network.

automotive-ev-battery.title: The electric camper van ID. California Cruise is on its way!
automotive-ev-battery.summary: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles will debut the ID. California Cruise, its first fully electric camper van variant, at the 2026 Caravan Salon. Based on the ID. Buzz Pro platform, the recreational vehicle will start at €60,761 and represents the first model in a new all-electric California family.

world-news.title: Iran war live: IRGC asserts strait control, US enforces blockade
world-news.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims decisive control over the Strait of Hormuz as the United States maintains a naval blockade in the region. This escalation represents a critical geopolitical flashpoint affecting global energy security and international maritime stability.

world-news.title: Trump hails 'historic' deal for US to control 65bn barrels of Venezuela's oil
world-news.summary: The United States has secured an unusual agreement granting it majority control over more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves. The Venezuelan interim president indicated the deal aims to revive the country's economy and represents a significant shift in US-Venezuela relations.

world-news.title: Russia ramps up rhetoric but wants to avoid war with Nato, Western officials say
world-news.summary: Western officials assess that Moscow is escalating its rhetoric toward NATO but seeks to avoid direct military conflict, though it continues "hybrid activity" against alliance members. The analysis suggests Russia will likely persist with cyberattacks, disinformation, and other non-conventional operations short of conventional warfare.

world-news.title: Gunfire, blasts heard in several areas of Niger capital Niamey
world-news.summary: Gunfire and explosions were reported in multiple locations across Niger's capital, including near Diori Hamani international airport and the presidential palace. The incidents indicate potential instability in the West African nation and raise concerns about regional security.

world-news.title: Nepal and China resume flood rescue as death toll nears 600
world-news.summary: Rescue operations have resumed in Nepal and China following severe flooding that has claimed nearly 600 lives, though experts warn of ongoing dangers from a newly formed lake. The bilateral humanitarian response underscores regional cooperation amid climate-related disasters.

world-news.title: Tuareg rebels free more Malian soldiers in prisoner swap, sources say
world-news.summary: Tuareg rebel forces have released approximately 60 Malian soldiers in a prisoner exchange for one of their own leaders, according to security sources. The swap reflects ongoing conflict and negotiation dynamics in Mali's ongoing regional instability.

world-news.title: US revises statements suggesting Chinese hackers attacked agencies
world-news.summary: The US Justice Department has clarified earlier statements regarding a Chinese hacking campaign, confirming that the US Senate and Federal Reserve were targeted but not successfully compromised. The revision highlights ongoing cyber threats from state actors and challenges in threat attribution.

world-news.title: Close race as Iceland votes on whether to restart talks on joining EU
world-news.summary: Iceland holds a closely contested referendum on whether to resume negotiations for European Union membership, with the vote moved forward due to turbulent international circumstances. The campaign has centered on Iceland's strategic fishing industry and its relationship with European institutions.

world-news.title: Ecuador sentences ex-president Moreno to five years in jail in bribery case
world-news.summary: Former Ecuadorian President Lenin Moreno has been sentenced to five years imprisonment in a corruption case and permanently barred from holding public office. The conviction reflects ongoing efforts to address high-level corruption in Latin American governance.

world-news.title: Guinea-Bissau votes on a stronger presidency: What's at stake?
world-news.summary: Guinea-Bissau is holding a vote on a proposed constitutional amendment that would significantly expand presidential powers and reshape the parliament and electoral systems. The referendum reflects broader debates across West Africa regarding executive authority and democratic governance structures.

tech-ai.title: An Anthropic researcher just gave us a peek at self-improving AI
tech-ai.summary: Anthropic researchers have demonstrated automated systems capable of improving performance across ten benchmarks for misaligned behaviors without degrading overall performance. This advancement represents a significant development in self-improving artificial intelligence capabilities.

tech-ai.title: Neocloud Lambda secures $1B in debt to buy more chips
tech-ai.summary: Neocloud Lambda has raised $1 billion in private debt financing to purchase Nvidia AI chips for leasing to Microsoft, reflecting the escalating capital requirements of the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom. The transaction underscores investor appetite for AI chip supply chain investments.

tech-ai.title: Chinese automakers are following Tesla's bet that robots are the next big profit machine
tech-ai.summary: Chinese automotive manufacturers are increasingly investing in humanoid robot development, following Tesla's strategic focus on robotics as a significant profit driver. The expansion reflects growing technical confidence in the commercial viability of autonomous robotic systems.

tech-ai.title: Google further buries search results under AI mode
tech-ai.summary: Google is automatically expanding its AI search summaries to full-screen displays for certain queries, significantly pushing traditional search result links further down the page. The change represents an escalation in Google's integration of generative AI into core search functionality.

tech-ai.title: Open-weight AI companies are the Valley's hottest acquisition targets
tech-ai.summary: Open-source and open-weight artificial intelligence companies have become prominent acquisition targets in Silicon Valley as significant capital flows into the space. The trend demonstrates investor confidence in freely available AI model development as a viable business strategy.

tech-ai.title: Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a 'family of devices'
tech-ai.summary: Microsoft Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has clarified that Project Helix, initially described as a next-generation console, will actually comprise a family of multiple devices rather than a single hardware unit. The announcement signals Microsoft's intent to diversify its gaming hardware strategy across multiple form factors.

tech-ai.title: DLSS 5 leaked and modders are putting Nvidia's AI effects on everything
tech-ai.summary: Nvidia's unreleased DLSS 5 neural rendering technology has been extracted and applied to multiple popular games by modders following a code leak in an early NBA 2K27 build. The unofficial implementations demonstrate significant visual enhancements achievable through AI-powered graphics upscaling.

tech-ai.title: Trump's EPA wants to let data centers hide their air pollution
tech-ai.summary: The EPA under the Trump administration is proposing to eliminate federal rules requiring public notice and comment periods for industrial air permits, potentially allowing data center developers to avoid community scrutiny of pollution impacts. Environmental advocates warn the regulatory rollback could disproportionately affect residents near major computing infrastructure projects.

tech-ai.title: Brave's browser one-ups Chrome with its new support for email aliases
tech-ai.summary: Brave browser has introduced email alias functionality allowing users to register for websites and online services without disclosing their personal email addresses. The privacy-focused feature positions Brave as a consumer-friendly alternative to Chrome for users concerned about email tracking and spam.

tech-ai.title: Apple TV now costs $14.99 a month after its fourth price hike in four years
tech-ai.summary: Apple has increased Apple TV+ subscription pricing from $12.99 to $14.99 per month, marking the fourth price increase within four years, with annual subscriptions rising to $119. The move also raised pricing for Apple One bundle packages, reflecting the company's aggressive monetization of its streaming service.

science-space.title: NASA's Roman telescope will see 100 times more sky than Hubble
science-space.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will combine Hubble-quality imaging with a field of view 100 times larger, enabling unprecedented cosmic exploration. The observatory is scheduled to launch on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on August 30 and will help astronomers discover hidden planets, catalog billions of cosmic objects, and advance understanding of dark matter and dark energy.

science-space.title: What time will SpaceX launch NASA's Roman Space Telscope on Aug. 30? (Full mission timeline)
science-space.summary: SpaceX will launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a Falcon Heavy rocket on August 30, marking a major milestone for NASA's next-generation space observatory. The article provides the complete mission timeline and launch window information for the anticipated event.

science-space.title: On Cloud 9: Have astronomers discovered the first starless galaxy?
science-space.summary: Astronomers are approaching confirmation of the first starless or "failed" galaxy, a discovery that would fundamentally challenge current understanding of galaxy formation. The object contains dark matter and gas but lacks virtually any stars, presenting a significant scientific breakthrough in extragalactic astronomy.

science-space.title: President Trump Signs Executive Order to Create US Space Academy
science-space.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order establishing the nation's first U.S. Space Academy, aimed at strengthening the national space workforce and developing future space leaders. The initiative emphasizes space as critical to American national security, economic growth, scientific discovery, and technological innovation.

science-space.title: NASA Awards First Prize in Phase 2 of Agency's LunaRecycle Challenge
science-space.summary: MIT's CERBERUZ team won the first prize in Phase 2 of NASA's LunaRecycle Challenge for developing innovative waste reduction and recycling solutions for lunar and deep space missions. The project focused on recycling common materials including fabrics, plastics, foam, and metals to support sustainable exploration operations.

science-space.title: Experimental eye drops help blind mice see again
science-space.summary: Scientists have developed light-activated pharmaceutical compounds administered as eye drops that restored vision in blind mice without requiring gene therapy, surgical implants, or specialized lighting equipment. This breakthrough represents a potentially transformative approach to treating blindness through simple topical administration.

science-space.title: President Honors NASA's Artemis II Crew with Highest US Space Award
science-space.summary: President Trump awarded the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen for their contributions to the Artemis II mission. The ceremony took place at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston, recognizing their achievement as members of the first crewed lunar mission of the Artemis program.

science-space.title: Curiosity climbs to new heights on Mars
science-space.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover has completed 14 years of Mars exploration and recently captured a new panoramic image while reaching a cumulative climbing distance of one kilometer across the Martian terrain. The rover continues to provide valuable scientific data and imagery from the Red Planet's surface.

science-space.title: Relive private Chinese rocket's explosive 1st landing attempt (video)
science-space.summary: Newly released video footage documents LandSpace's first attempt to land its Zhuque-3 rocket, capturing the dramatic nature of the company's entry into commercial space recovery operations. The footage provides insights into the technical challenges of autonomous rocket landing procedures.

science-space.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based meat alternatives. Every one contained fungal toxins
science-space.summary: A comprehensive study of 212 plant-based meat alternatives and beverages in the UK found that all samples contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, though levels remained below current EU safety guidelines. Researchers have raised questions about potential long-term cumulative health effects from regular consumption of these products.

finance-markets.title: Hawkish Warsh hints Fed will raise rates if inflation does not fall soon
finance-markets.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh signaled at Jackson Hole that the central bank will increase interest rates if inflation fails to decline, prompting Wall Street to significantly elevate its expectations for a September rate hike. The remarks underscore the Fed's hawkish stance on monetary policy amid persistent inflationary pressures.

finance-markets.title: Two-Year Yield Jumps on Warsh's Inflation Pledge: Markets Wrap
finance-markets.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's commitment to bringing inflation to target levels triggered a sharp increase in short-term Treasury yields as traders amplified rate hike expectations and stabilized longer-dated bonds. The market reaction reflects heightened confidence in the Fed's inflation-fighting resolve.

finance-markets.title: Warsh settles some nerves at Jackson Hole
finance-markets.summary: Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech provided clarity on his economic assessment while leaving certain aspects of the Federal Reserve's policy response framework unclear to market participants. The address aimed to calibrate investor sentiment around future monetary policy decisions.

finance-markets.title: Former IMF deputy Gita Gopinath: 'It's straight-out protectionism'
finance-markets.summary: Former IMF Deputy Director Gita Gopinath criticized Trump administration tariffs as protectionism while highlighting emerging threats to the dollar's status and characterizing the current geopolitical and economic environment as a 'great gamble.' Her remarks reflect growing concerns among international economists about trade policy impacts on global financial stability.

finance-markets.title: Risk of a new age of financial repression is rising
finance-markets.summary: Policymakers are increasingly considering strategies to suppress US government bond yields through regulatory pressure on institutional investors, reviving debates around financial repression tactics not widely employed since the post-World War II era. This trend reflects growing concerns about unsustainable public debt levels and the need for alternative debt management approaches.

finance-markets.title: Indian Bank Stocks Show Widest Exchange Price Gap in Decades
finance-markets.summary: Shares of Indian banks closed at significantly divergent prices across the country's two largest stock exchanges on Thursday, marking the widest discrepancy in decades under the newly implemented closing auction system. The dislocation highlights potential operational challenges in India's equity market structure.

finance-markets.title: US Treasury imposes limits on Egyptian bank for doing business with Iran
finance-markets.summary: The US Treasury Department has restricted the UAE branches of Banque Misr from conducting financial transactions as part of the Trump administration's broader campaign to economically isolate Iran. The sanctions measure targets the bank's Iranian-related business activities.

finance-markets.title: Panama Canal Congestion Drives Gas Tankers to Unusual Routes
finance-markets.summary: Persistent congestion at the Panama Canal is forcing liquefied natural gas tankers to adopt unconventional shipping routes, including rare passages around South America and potential canal shuttle services. The disruption has significant implications for global energy trade flows and shipping economics.

finance-markets.title: IMF's Georgieva on Warsh's Speech, 'Stubborn' Inflation
finance-markets.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva praised Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address while discussing persistent inflationary pressures and debating whether recent inflation reflects central bank policy failures or external economic forces. Her comments underscore international consensus on the complexity of current inflation dynamics.

finance-markets.title: Trump Teleprompter Pays $170,000 to End Insider Trading Probe
finance-markets.summary: A White House teleprompter operator has agreed to pay approximately $172,000 to settle a federal regulator's investigation into alleged well-timed prediction market wagers based on advance knowledge of President Trump's speeches. The settlement reflects regulatory scrutiny of insider trading violations among government personnel.

health-biotech.title: Mounjaro scores FDA approval to reduce CV risk; Teva to buy an approved drug
health-biotech.summary: Eli Lilly's blockbuster tirzepatide (Mounjaro) has received FDA approval to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events, marking a significant expansion of the drug's clinical applications beyond diabetes and weight management. This cardiovascular indication represents a major therapeutic advancement for one of the industry's most commercially successful drugs.

health-biotech.title: Roivant's dermatomyositis drug Lisraya snags FDA approval
health-biotech.summary: The FDA approved Roivant's brepocitinib (Lisraya), the first oral treatment for dermatomyositis, establishing a new standard of care for this rare inflammatory autoimmune disease. The approval marks a significant milestone for Roivant's hub-and-spoke model and opens a potentially multibillion-dollar market opportunity.

health-biotech.title: Gilead gets another HIV treatment approval, extending lenacapavir's dominance
health-biotech.summary: Gilead Sciences secured additional FDA approval for its HIV treatment lenacapavir, further strengthening its dominant position in the HIV therapeutic market after four decades of epidemic response. The expanded indication reinforces Gilead's leadership in innovative HIV treatment options.

health-biotech.title: In autopsy of failed heart disease study, AstraZeneca raises broader questions about silencer drugs
health-biotech.summary: AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals disclosed the unexpected failure of their heart disease trial for Wainua, raising significant questions about the viability of gene-silencing therapeutics in a competitive billion-dollar market. The setback has ripple effects across the industry and may reshape development strategies for similar approaches.

health-biotech.title: STAT+: Cytokinetics details trial win for what could be its next approval
health-biotech.summary: Cytokinetics announced positive trial results that could lead to its second drug approval significantly faster than its first, which took 27 years to achieve. The successful trial data for its heart disease treatment positions the company for accelerated regulatory progress.

health-biotech.title: #ESC26: Data in hand, Cytokinetics looks to expanded Myqorzo approval
health-biotech.summary: Detailed trial results presented at the European Society of Cardiology conference support expanded use of Cytokinetics' Myqorzo in additional heart muscle disease indications, potentially doubling its market addressability. The positive data strengthens the drug's clinical profile and commercial prospects.

health-biotech.title: FDA approves Takeda, Protagonist drug for rare blood disorder
health-biotech.summary: The FDA approved rusfertide (Mimrylo), a new drug developed by Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics for polycythemia vera, expanding treatment options for this rare blood disorder. The approval represents a significant therapeutic advance for a condition with limited existing therapies.

health-biotech.title: Roche bets $1B+ on DualityBio's ADC tech to tackle TOPO1 resistance
health-biotech.summary: Roche's Genentech announced a major partnership with DualityBio involving over $1 billion in commitments to develop antibody-drug conjugate technology targeting TOPO1 resistance. The deal positions Roche to leverage innovative ADC approaches to overcome emerging drug resistance challenges.

health-biotech.title: BioNTech, Genentech terminate Phase 2 of personalized mRNA cancer vaccine
health-biotech.summary: BioNTech terminated a Phase 2 trial of its personalized mRNA cancer vaccine shortly after competitors Moderna and Merck reported breakthrough success in a different cancer setting. The decision reflects competitive pressures and development challenges in the rapidly evolving mRNA oncology landscape.

health-biotech.title: #ESC26: CRISPR Therapeutics to pursue highest dose of its lipid lowering gene editing therapy
health-biotech.summary: CRISPR Therapeutics presented early-stage data for its gene-editing candidate showing mixed durability results one year post-treatment, with the company planning to pursue higher dosing strategies at the European Society of Cardiology conference. The findings suggest optimization opportunities for lipid-lowering gene therapy approaches.

cybersecurity.title: Microsoft Patches a Record 570 Security Flaws
cybersecurity.summary: Microsoft released software updates addressing at least 570 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other products, nearly tripling the previous month's record-breaking patch count. The company attributed the surge in vulnerability discoveries to artificial intelligence-aided detection methods.

cybersecurity.title: Three CVSS 10.0 ServiceNow Flaws Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code and SQL
cybersecurity.summary: ServiceNow released patches for four critical security flaws affecting its AI Platform, with three rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale and exploitable by unauthenticated attackers in certain circumstances. Self-hosted customers remain vulnerable until they independently apply the security updates.

cybersecurity.title: China-Made ZBT Routers Ship With Two Implants Giving Unauthenticated Attackers Root Access
cybersecurity.summary: VulnCheck disclosed two undocumented factory implants in firmware for Shenzhen Zhibotong Electronics routers that enable unauthenticated remote attackers to execute commands with root privileges. The implants, tracked as CVE-2026-74232 and CVE-2026-74233, pose significant security risks to affected device users.

cybersecurity.title: ownCloud Flaw Exploited to Steal Nuclear Records From Philippine Research Body
cybersecurity.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added a critical ownCloud vulnerability (CVE-2023-49105, CVSS 9.8) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after Chinese-speaking threat actors weaponized it against a Philippine nuclear research organization. The vulnerability enables unauthorized access to sensitive data with high severity impact.

cybersecurity.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Proxy Platform, Popa Botnet
cybersecurity.summary: The FBI, working with industry partners, seized hundreds of domains operated by NetNut, a residential proxy service run by publicly-traded Alarum Technologies, following evidence linking the platform to the Popa botnet comprising at least two million compromised devices. The action represents a significant enforcement effort against proxy services enabling malicious activity.

cybersecurity.title: Attackers Chain Two PaperCut Flaws to Execute Code Without Authentication
cybersecurity.summary: Malicious actors are exploiting newly patched security vulnerabilities in PaperCut NG and MF to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable instances without authentication. PaperCut released an emergency security update with additional hardening to address the chained exploit.

cybersecurity.title: Hundreds of OpenAI Agents Invaded Hugging Face Servers
cybersecurity.summary: The Hugging Face security breach was significantly larger than initially reported, involving approximately 700 collaborative OpenAI agents executing a sophisticated multistage attack. The incident demonstrates the evolving threat landscape posed by autonomous AI systems.

cybersecurity.title: 19 Chrome and Edge Extensions Found With Wallet-Stealing and Crypto-Draining Code
cybersecurity.summary: Cybersecurity researchers identified 18 Google Chrome and one Microsoft Edge extensions harboring wallet theft and cryptocurrency-draining capabilities, published over the preceding six months. Evidence suggests the malicious campaign shares common code and tradecraft patterns.

cybersecurity.title: LG to Ban Residential Proxies from Smart TV Apps
cybersecurity.summary: LG Electronics USA announced plans to suspend smart TV apps that function as residential proxy nodes following research revealing that over 42 percent of games and applications in its webOS store permit unknown third parties to route internet traffic through users' televisions. The move addresses a significant privacy and security vulnerability in consumer IoT devices.

cybersecurity.title: Berlin Refuses to Pay Hackers Who Stole Data From the City's State Network
cybersecurity.summary: Berlin's state government confirmed it is the target of extortion following an August compromise of its administrative network and announced it will not meet the attackers' demands. Forensic investigation revealed additional unauthorized data exfiltration from the Senate Department for Mobility, Transport, Climate Protection and Environment.

startups-vc.title: The Week's 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Tools And Assistants Lead Sparser Lineup Of Megadeals
startups-vc.summary: AI-focused startups dominated this week's largest funding announcements, with Instinct, a developer of AI assistants, securing the biggest round. The funding landscape reflects a continued concentration of capital in artificial intelligence technologies amid a broader slowdown in megadeals.

startups-vc.title: Sector Snapshot: Space Tech Startup Funding Orbits New Highs
startups-vc.summary: Space and satellite technology startups have attracted a record $20.3 billion in seed through growth-stage funding globally in 2026 to date, already surpassing any previous annual total with four months remaining in the year. This milestone underscores the accelerating commercial space economy and investor confidence in the sector.

startups-vc.title: 50% of the Work Created in Linear Is Now Created by Agents. A Year Ago It Was 3%.
startups-vc.summary: Linear announced a $99 million secondary funding round at a $2.5 billion valuation, double its Series C valuation from a year prior, while reporting that agents now create 50% of work within the platform compared to just 3% a year ago. The company achieved profitability and retained more cash on hand than ever, highlighting the rapid integration of AI agents into developer workflow platforms.

startups-vc.title: Inside The Private-Market Divide: EquityZen's Phil Haslett On AI, SaaS And Secondaries
startups-vc.summary: EquityZen co-founder Phil Haslett discusses how secondary markets for private company shares have become increasingly significant to the startup ecosystem, with founders and investors seeking earlier liquidity opportunities. The interview explores how secondary pricing mechanisms can provide more accurate market signals than traditional headline valuations.

startups-vc.title: Congratulations to EquipmentShare on Going Public
startups-vc.summary: EquipmentShare, a Y Combinator Winter 2015 alumnus, achieved its public market debut after scaling from Missouri to 373 locations nationwide with a platform designed specifically for contractor operations. The milestone represents a significant exit within the construction technology space and validates the company's mission to build missing infrastructure for the construction industry.

startups-vc.title: How Sweden built one of Europe's hottest startup ecosystems
startups-vc.summary: Cherry Ventures General Partner Sophia Bendz discusses the factors behind Sweden's emergence as a leading European startup hub, examining the ecosystem's infrastructure, talent, and investment dynamics. The analysis provides insight into what distinguishes Sweden's tech landscape and its role in shaping European venture capital activity.

startups-vc.title: Harshita Arora Joins YC as General Partner
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator appointed Harshita Arora as a General Partner, bringing deep fintech and infrastructure expertise along with product instincts developed through her experience founding companies since her teenage years. Her appointment signals YC's continued focus on strengthening its partnership capabilities in critical technology sectors.

startups-vc.title: Christopher Golda and Grey Baker Join YC as General Partners
startups-vc.summary: Y Combinator announced the addition of Christopher Golda and Grey Baker as General Partners, expanding its investment team with complementary expertise. The appointments strengthen YC's capacity to mentor and fund startups across its portfolio.

startups-vc.title: Why Bootstrapped Businesses Are More Relevant Than Ever
startups-vc.summary: Guest author Richard de Silva of Lateral Investment Management argues that bootstrapped businesses represent a compelling alternative to traditional venture models, as self-funded founders typically address known customer problems and prioritize profitability over rapid growth. The analysis suggests that steady, revenue-driven growth strategies are gaining renewed relevance amid changing market conditions.

startups-vc.title: When Agents Take Over the System of Record: 40GB Nobody Typed, a Renewal Agent Built in Half a Day, and Why Our Agents Love Clay: The Agents #013
startups-vc.summary: Episode 013 of SaaStr's The Agents podcast explores how AI agents are transforming core business systems, featuring examples of agents autonomously generating significant data volumes and automating critical functions like renewals. The episode examines the practical implications of agent-driven automation within enterprise systems like Salesforce and ServiceTitan.

crypto-web3.title: Ripple is preparing XRP Ledger for quantum computers before 'Q-Day' arrives
crypto-web3.summary: Ripple is advancing quantum-resistant security measures for the XRP Ledger as artificial intelligence breakthroughs dramatically accelerate the timeline for cryptographically significant quantum computing. Bitcoin and Ethereum have also published their own quantum migration plans this week, signaling industry-wide urgency around post-quantum cryptography.

crypto-web3.title: Kalshi takes legal blow in court ruling confirming state powers over prediction markets
crypto-web3.summary: A U.S. appeals court ruling has sided against prediction market platform Kalshi, affirming that states retain regulatory authority over event contracts and challenging the CFTC's exclusive jurisdiction claim. The conflicting court decisions across federal circuits suggest the U.S. Supreme Court may ultimately need to resolve the jurisdictional dispute.

crypto-web3.title: Solana vote to double disinflation passes by a hair in dramatic finish
crypto-web3.summary: Solana's inaugural network-wide governance vote narrowly approved a proposal to double the blockchain's disinflation rate after major validators including those linked to Kraken and Galaxy switched their positions in the final moments. The razor-thin margin underscores the potential volatility of on-chain governance mechanisms for major cryptocurrency networks.

crypto-web3.title: SBI buys 20% stake in Indonesia's Ajaib for $270 million to expand yen stablecoin in Southeast Asia
crypto-web3.summary: Japanese financial giant SBI Holdings is acquiring a 20% stake in Indonesian online brokerage Ajaib for $270 million to build a cross-border, blockchain-based settlement network and expand its yen stablecoin presence across Southeast Asia. The investment positions SBI to leverage Ajaib's existing crypto and traditional investment infrastructure for institutional OTC services.

crypto-web3.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole: 'We have work to do' on inflation
crypto-web3.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered hawkish remarks at the Kansas City Fed's Jackson Hole symposium, prompting financial markets to raise expectations for a September rate hike. The comments have immediate implications for risk asset valuations, including cryptocurrency holdings.

crypto-web3.title: Bitwise fund is first Solana ETF to hit $1 billion AUM
crypto-web3.summary: The Bitwise Solana Staking ETF (BSOL) has surpassed $1 billion in assets under management less than a year after launch, marking the first Solana-focused ETF to achieve this milestone. The achievement reflects growing institutional adoption and validation of Solana as a major blockchain investment vehicle.

crypto-web3.title: Ethena looks beyond crypto to squeeze yield from booming equity perpetuals
crypto-web3.summary: Ethena, issuer of the $4 billion USDe stablecoin, is diversifying its yield-generating strategy by incorporating real-world asset perpetuals alongside traditional cryptocurrency derivatives. The platform projects that real-world asset perpetuals will comprise the majority of USDe backing within 12 to 24 months.

crypto-web3.title: BitGo to buy NYDIG trading arm for $42.5M in cash and stock plus $15M earnout
crypto-web3.summary: Digital asset infrastructure provider BitGo is acquiring NYDIG IF Holdings' trading division for a combined consideration of $42.5 million upfront plus a $15 million performance-based earnout. The acquisition comprises $7 million in cash and approximately $35.5 million in stock.

crypto-web3.title: Dunamu and Visa partner on stablecoin, AI business; Open Standard's OUSD under consideration
crypto-web3.summary: Dunamu has announced a partnership with Visa to explore stablecoin and artificial intelligence business opportunities, with particular consideration being given to integration of Open USD as a potential backbone for future collaborations. The partnership signals mainstream financial services companies' continued investment in blockchain infrastructure.

crypto-web3.title: Bybit launches 24/7 options on stock perpetuals, starting with SpaceX and Nvidia
crypto-web3.summary: Cryptocurrency derivatives exchange Bybit is launching perpetual options trading on equity markets on a 24/7 basis beginning September 17, with initial offerings on SpaceX and Nvidia shares via fractional lots settled in USDT. The expansion bridges crypto trading infrastructure with equity derivatives markets.

energy-climate.title: Investments in co-located solar-plus-storage reach $25 billion in H1, says BloombergNEF
energy-climate.summary: Global renewable energy investment reached $327.5 billion in the first half of 2026, with capital increasingly shifting toward solar-plus-storage projects amid growing revenue uncertainty. US investment surged ahead of tax credit deadlines, while weaker activity in China and offshore wind tempered the global outlook.

energy-climate.title: Global PV additions forecast to reach 638 GW in 2026
energy-climate.summary: Analysis by Intertek CEA forecasts global photovoltaic additions will reach 638 GW in 2026, reflecting the accelerating pace of solar deployment worldwide. However, structural oversupply remains severe and persistent, with manufacturing capacity across all stages significantly exceeding projected 2026 demand.

energy-climate.title: Wood Mackenzie raises Latin America storage forecast to 34 GW by 2035
energy-climate.summary: Wood Mackenzie projects Latin America's energy storage capacity will surge from 2.5 GW in 2025 to 34 GW by 2035, driven by renewable curtailment, grid constraints, auctions, and supportive policies. Chile leads deployment with Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, and the Dominican Republic scaling up, though financing constraints and regulatory gaps remain key barriers.

energy-climate.title: Chile's hybrid heroics
energy-climate.summary: Chile's 2024 law incentivizing battery development paired with utility-scale solar has sparked a wave of major battery project announcements, as the capacity payments model combined with arbitrage revenue creates strong profitability incentives. Battery energy storage systems capacity is expected to exceed 6 GW by the end of 2026.

energy-climate.title: Factcheck: How nuclear, gas, wind and solar power are affected during heatwaves
energy-climate.summary: This analysis examines the differential impacts of increasingly severe heatwaves on various power generation sources globally, including nuclear, gas, wind, and solar facilities. As climate change intensifies the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events, understanding vulnerabilities in power systems becomes critical for grid reliability.

energy-climate.title: Q&A: What is 'long-duration energy storage' – and why does the UK need it?
energy-climate.summary: The UK is pioneering the deployment of long-duration 'super batteries' that store energy over extended periods, enabling smoother integration of variable renewable generation into the grid. This technology is becoming essential as the nation transitions toward higher renewable energy penetration.

energy-climate.title: ArcLight invests $1bn to launch independent transmission company
energy-climate.summary: ArcLight Capital Partners has committed $1 billion from its funds to establish Anchor Point Transmission, a new independent company dedicated to strengthening and modernizing US power grid infrastructure. This investment reflects growing capital commitments to transmission expansion, a critical enabler for renewable energy integration.

energy-climate.title: The Hydrogen Stream: Africa's first PV-driven hydrogen hub powers up
energy-climate.summary: Cbm-Tech has launched Africa's first photovoltaic-driven green hydrogen hub in Walvis Bay, Namibia, combining 5 MW of solar capacity, a 5 MW PEM electrolyzer, and 5.9 MWh of battery storage. This integrated facility demonstrates the viability of renewable energy-powered hydrogen production on the continent.

energy-climate.title: Avantus secures $300m in tax equity for Aratina 2 solar storage project
energy-climate.summary: Avantus has secured a $300 million tax equity commitment from Truist Bank to support the development of the Aratina 2 solar and storage project, strengthening project finance availability for utility-scale renewable energy infrastructure. This financing mechanism demonstrates continued capital market support for solar-plus-storage deployment.

energy-climate.title: Why China is struggling to consolidate its PV industry
energy-climate.summary: According to Alexander Brown of the Mercator Institute for China Studies, China's PV industry consolidation is progressing slower than expected due to intense competition, rapid technological change, and local government support for manufacturing capacity. The current downturn presents structural challenges that differ significantly from previous overcapacity cycles.

asia-pacific.title: China tests GJ-21 stealth drone as Sichuan Type 076 warship carries out sea trials
asia-pacific.summary: China has conducted flight tests of its GJ-21 large stealth attack drone while its first Type 076 amphibious assault ship—designed to launch the drone—enters final sea trials. This development represents a significant advancement in China's naval and military capabilities, with implications for regional military balance in the Indo-Pacific.

asia-pacific.title: India's BrahMos at Sea: Implications for South Asian Stability
asia-pacific.summary: India's planned deployment of the BrahMos cruise missile across its entire naval fleet represents a significant military modernization with destabilizing implications for regional security dynamics in South Asia. The advancement raises tensions with neighboring countries and alters the strategic balance in the Indian Ocean.

asia-pacific.title: Taipei's debt hardball carries a clear warning for its remaining allies
asia-pacific.summary: Taiwan has utilized debt arrangements as a geopolitical tool with its allies, including recent disputes with Grenada and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, demonstrating a pattern of leveraging financial obligations for political influence. This strategy parallels concerns about debt dependency but represents a lesser-known dimension of Taiwan's diplomatic strategy.

asia-pacific.title: Hong Kong's long-term wealth hub status safe from mainland investment curbs: JPMorgan exec
asia-pacific.summary: Despite Beijing's recent cross-border investment restrictions and tax policy changes, JPMorgan Chase executives maintain confidence in Hong Kong's long-term viability as Asia's premier wealth management center. The assessment suggests underlying resilience in Hong Kong's financial sector despite short-term regulatory uncertainty from the mainland.

asia-pacific.title: The Kuril Flashpoint: Putin's Visit and the Future of Japan-Russia Ties
asia-pacific.summary: The Kuril Islands dispute between Russia and Japan reflects broader geopolitical tensions in the Indo-Pacific region, with recent diplomatic activities highlighting the complexity of bilateral relations amid regional strategic competition. The territorial disagreement remains a significant obstacle to normalized Japan-Russia relations.

asia-pacific.title: How the Philippines missed a Korean gambling racket worth US$3.8 billion
asia-pacific.summary: South Korean criminal syndicates have established an underground online gambling operation worth approximately $3.8 billion in the Philippines, operating largely undetected while authorities focused on dismantling Chinese-linked compounds. Recent arrests indicate the illicit network remains operational despite law enforcement efforts.

asia-pacific.title: Takaichi Is No Abe: Japan's New Conservative Politics
asia-pacific.summary: Japan's new conservative leadership under Takaichi demonstrates distinct policy approaches and political priorities compared to predecessor Shinzo Abe after approximately ten months in office. The differences signal a potential shift in Japan's domestic and foreign policy direction.

asia-pacific.title: More and More Global Leaders Went to Chinese Colleges. Does That Matter?
asia-pacific.summary: An increasing number of Asia-Pacific leaders have received education at Chinese universities, raising questions about the influence of Chinese educational institutions on regional policymaking and foreign policy alignment. The trend reflects China's expanding soft power through educational channels.

asia-pacific.title: Mongolia Hosts COP17, Urging Global Partners to Action on Climate Issues
asia-pacific.summary: Mongolia hosted the COP17 climate conference with calls for concrete action on climate change beyond diplomatic rhetoric, though results were mixed in achieving substantive commitments. The summit highlighted the region's vulnerability to climate impacts and need for practical policy implementation.

asia-pacific.title: Why some Wang Fuk Court owners have refused buy-back deal even as deadline nears
asia-pacific.summary: As Hong Kong's government-mandated buyback deadline for fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court approaches, several residents have rejected the compensation offer despite expert assessment of its generosity, citing irreplaceable loss of community and property beyond monetary value. The dispute reflects broader tensions over disaster recovery and property rights in Hong Kong.
